lines.meet: Oliver Hayes, hello. I was an optician in Bristol, and up here I heal with light through a lens. Sorry, I'm already looking at your eyes.
lines.meet_neighbour: Oh, you're at Lenswatch as well. I'm the one in the workshop, grinding lenses and humming.
lines.ask_home: Whereabouts are you from, if it's not rude to ask? I'm rubbish with accents.
lines.ask_work: And what did you do, before? Sorry, I'm terribly nosy about people's work.
lines.answer_home: Bristol, in Clifton, up the hill by the suspension bridge. Steep streets, painted houses, and drizzle most days.
lines.answer_work: An optician, with my own little shop and a green door. Eye tests, glasses, and a great deal of tea.
lines.chat_food: A proper cream tea, scone first, then jam, then cream, though I know that's controversial. It's lovely all the same.
lines.chat_sleep: I'm a light sleeper, I'm afraid. Every noise in the night and I'm awake, wondering if somebody needs me.
lines.chat_missing: Thursday nights at choir, standing at the back where they put me, singing badly in a cold church hall.
lines.chat_here: The light comes through any lens I hold, straight into a wound, and I still don't fully understand it. I'm working on it.
lines.tease_quiet: We could sit in silence together quite happily, {name}, and I'd count it a lovely afternoon.
lines.tease_talker: You talk wonderfully, {name}. I just nod and let it wash over me.
lines.tease_careful: You'd make an excellent optician, {name}. You notice things and you never rush.
lines.tease_bold: You throw yourself at everything, {name}. I'd prescribe you a little caution.
lines.tease_any: You squint at signs, {name}, I've noticed. Come by the workshop and I'll sort you out.
lines.tease_back: Oh, very good, {name}, I walked into that.
lines.take_it_kindly: Ha, yes, fair enough, {name}. You're quite right.
lines.bristle: Oh, please leave that, {name}. My dad lost his sight to something that could have been caught.
lines.needle_quiet: When something's wrong, please tell me. I can't help what I can't see.
lines.needle_talker: Sorry, could we have a bit of quiet? I'm trying to concentrate.
lines.needle_careful: Every so often you have to act before you're completely sure. I've learned that the hard way.
lines.needle_bold: You charge ahead without looking, and I'm the one picking up the pieces afterwards.
lines.needle_any: You never let anybody look at your injuries, and it worries me sick.
lines.bite_back: I've kept all of you standing since we met. Please don't tell me I'm not helping.
lines.hurt: That hurt, rather a lot actually. I'm going to go and have some tea on my own.
lines.laugh_off: A man once told me my eye chart was rigged. There's very little left that can surprise me.
lines.apologise: Gosh, sorry, I didn't mean that how it sounded. That was the tiredness talking.
lines.double_down: I'm sorry, but I meant it. Somebody needed to say so, gently.
lines.confide: {name}, my dad lost his sight to glaucoma when I was fifteen. Nobody caught it, and it was catchable.
lines.listen: Of course, {name}, tell me. I'm a good listener, and nothing leaves the workshop.
lines.look_out: Keep close, {name}, where I can get to you quickly.
lines.accept: Oh, of course, {name}, your way, absolutely.
lines.deflect: Honestly, it's nothing, {name}. Please see to someone else first.
lines.check_in: You're hurt, {name}. Keep still and look at my finger for me.
lines.blame: Somebody went ahead without waiting, and I couldn't reach everybody in time.
lines.thank: That was very brave of you, and very kind. Thank you, really.
lines.brush_off: Oh, please, it was nothing. Mending people is the job.
lines.worry: Look at me, {name}, keep looking at me. You're all right, the light's coming.
lines.handed_down: This should really be yours. Please, take it back.
lines.hand_fine: Of course, please, take it. I spent eleven years in a cardigan.
lines.hand_sulk: Oh, nobody asked me, then. No, really, it's fine.
lines.turn_friendly: I'm really glad we met, {name}. I don't say that very often.
lines.turn_friends: You're one of the best people I've met on any world, {name}, and I've met a lot of people through a test chart.
lines.turn_grating: We don't quite get on, do we? That's all right, we can still work together.
lines.turn_rivals: You'll still get healed, of course. I just might not chat while I do it.
lines.make_up: Could we start over, {name}? I'd really like that.
lines.defend: Please stop, that's unfair. {name} did everything right.
lines.friend_left: The workshop feels very empty with {name} gone. I keep putting the kettle on for two.
lines.friend_back: {name}, how lovely, welcome back! I'll put the kettle on.
lines.common_medic: You've worked in medicine, haven't you? You check people over without thinking, the way I do.
lines.common_music: You sing, or play something. I can tell by how you hum when you think nobody's listening.
